newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Diesel steady to a tad softer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Diesel steady to a tad softer.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were steady to slightly weaker at midday on Thursday amid softer crude values and moderate buying interest, brokers said.
They said the gas oil market is flat to slightly in contango with the jet fuel/gas oil regrade widening slightly.

Traders said the physical market remained under pressure with only one deal seen on Wednesday between two Japanese traders at $25.00 per barrel with sellers continuing to be in abundance and putting pressure on the market.
June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $24.70-$24.85 per barrel, almost flat from Wednesday, with July indicated at $24.75-$24.90. July traded at $24.83.
Traders said they did not expect to get much support from India's gas oil tender for July with projections of 400,000-600,000 tonnes to be awarded.
India bought 315,000 tonnes in June and 840,000 tonnes in May.
China was also still not expected to give much support to the market as stocks on the mainland and in Hong Kong are still high, traders said.

But some support came from Sri Lanka which has issued yet another tender to buy 220,000 barrels of gas oil and 80,000 barrels of jet fuel for June 21-22 delivery. Sri Lanka already has two other tenders for June which was awarded earlier.
The additional requirements were due to an unscheduled shutdown at its 55,000-barrel-per-day refinery from the first week of June.
Traders said the fuel oil market remained steady despite the soft undertone on the physical market on Wednesday amid an overnight drop in crudes. Buying interest was thin.
Swaps for June was seen at $99/$100.50 and July at $98.00/$99.25 almost largely unchanged from the previous day.
